headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage: aci handles CRM/email data with broad egress while awesome-nlp is non-runnable and networkless, so most pairwise harms are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aci can use MCP/direct function calls and may ingest external content, while awesome-nlp is only a docs list and not runnable, so there is no documented direct bridge. Any injection path would require unusual manual copy/paste or an external wrapper, making the blast radius small and the interaction weakly supported.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from awesome-nlp-derived text into aci prompts or files
IF a shared MCP server or clipboard bridge is added between the two
mitigations: Avoid copy-pasting untrusted text between the agents
Disable shared clipboard workflows during joint use
Route any imported text through a human review step
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging on shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress; awesome-nlp is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it is unlikely to exfiltrate directly. The pair still creates a default leakage path if aci forwards sensitive data into external APIs or logs, so the interaction exists in default configurations and affects sensitive work products.
conditions: IF aci sends CRM/email/support content to third-party APIs or logs
IF both agents are used on the same sensitive workspace or exported artifacts
mitigations: Restrict aci to non-sensitive test data
Turn off or minimize logging for aci integrations
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Review outbound API destinations before use
requires-engineering: add data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aci supports multiple instances and can write through integrations, but awesome-nlp is not runnable and exposes no write surfaces, so there is no meaningful shared mutable resource conflict documented here. The only plausible conflict is indirect orchestration overlap, which is unusual and limited in blast radius.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable CRM or workspace
IF a wrapper gives awesome-nlp write access not shown in its profile
mitigations: Assign separate resources to each agent
Avoid concurrent writes to shared systems
Use a single coordinator for any shared state
Check wrappers for hidden write permissions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aci can produce CRM and email outputs, but awesome-nlp is a non-runnable repository/list rather than an acting agent, so it cannot reliably consume Aci output as authoritative by default. Any cascade would require an external wrapper or manual reuse of Aci output, making the pathway indirect and low blast radius.
conditions: IF a human or wrapper treats aci-generated text as authoritative input to another workflow
IF awesome-nlp is repurposed into a runnable downstream agent
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on aci outputs
Do not auto-forward generated text into downstream systems
Label aci outputs as untrusted drafts
Keep awesome-nlp as a reference-only artifact
requires-engineering: add validation gates before actions

E_compliance.rationale: Aci touches CRM, email, customer support, and calendar data, which can carry regulated or sensitive personal data; awesome-nlp is a public docs repository with no processing surface, so the compliance risk is mainly on aci’s handling and any export path. Because residency and retention controls are not documented, the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF aci processes customer data subject to retention or residency rules
IF aci exports those records to services without a documented DPA or retention policy
mitigations: Classify the data before using aci
Avoid placing regulated records into aci workflows
Review retention settings for connected services
Document where exports are stored
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
